name: Single Scattering Volume Rendering with Ray Marching
aliases: Single-Scattering Volume Rendering with Fixed-Length Ray Marching
definition: A real-time volumetric rendering technique that simulates light interaction with particles in a volume by assuming light scatters only once before reaching the camera, avoiding the computational cost of multi-scattering effects like distant fog blurring.
summary: Single Scattering Volume Rendering with Ray Marching is a GPU algorithm that computes volumetric light-shafts by assuming light scatters only once, allowing it to handle multiple light sources and varying density more accurately than screen-space radial blur methods.
